title: Instruction selection = tiling the DAG
summary_caption: Selection is tiling: cover the DAG with target tiles at least cost. x86's memory-operand tile covers load+add in one instruction; a RISC tile set needs two.

frames.caption: Build, step 1 — the note's IR pair (%v = load ptr %p; %r = add %v, %x) enters SelectionDAG. Its leaves are the incoming values %p and %x.
Build, step 2 — each IR op becomes an SDNode: the load reads %p, and the add uses the load's result %v plus %x. One DAG per basic block.
Legalize + combine — i32 load and i32 add are both legal on x86, so nothing needs rewriting here; the DAG is unchanged.
Select — the matcher starts at the DAG's root, the add, and asks: which TableGen tiles from x86's .td files match here?
Candidate tile 1 — the register-register add (ADD32rr) covers only the add node. The load would then need its own instruction: 2 total.
Candidate tile 2 — the add-from-memory tile (ADD32rm) matches add(load %p, %x): ONE tile covering BOTH IR ops.
The bigger, cheaper covering wins (the textbook name for this greedy choice is maximal munch): the load folds into the add's addressing mode.
Emit — the pair becomes ONE machine instruction, add %x, (%p). Slot 2 stays empty: two IR ops, one tile, one instruction.
Same DAG, different target — a RISC machine has no memory-operand add, so the big tile simply does not exist in its .td files.
Selection falls back to two smaller tiles: a load, then a register add. Two instructions — the target's tile set decides the covering.
